One of the things that kenshi gets right, is the grinding. The entire game is built around grinding. This may sound horrible at first, until you try it. grinding in this game is fun. It takes the best aspects of RPG grinding, and the best aspects or RTS resource gathering, and combines the two.

But this takes a while to understand, and can be tedious at first.

The first grind you will find now, is not farming, but mining. Why? because you will need to mine the copper and iron resources located all of the map, to sell the ore for food.

mining ore will level up both manual labor AND strength, in that carrying the ore will help guys with low strength get stronger.

you will use this to raise enough money to pay for any food and materials you need to build your base.

Next is combat. Combat in this game is treacherous to level up, as being ko'd now has the risk of both robbery and enslavement. the solution is to "guard" towns. This has several benefits in that you are not fighting tough battles alone, and if you buy a house in town, you have a place to recover from your injuries.

Depending on how you start, i would recommend in most cases, setting up in a town. buy a building, build a bed and a research bench in it. This gives you a short distance to buy and story materials needed for farming research. After all, you can not really farm until you have researched wheat farming. Once you have wheat farming, you will be more than ready to build a sustainable base almost anywhere.

Regardless of anything else you read, just remember one basic thing about this game: you will grind. It will be fun, and going from a naked, severally beaten person in the desert into a warlord feared by all is really something.
Surviving kenshi: The grind is the game.
